name: Question 6
worked_solution:
Let $u=6x+6.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{6}\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that $x=\frac{1}{6}(u-6).$ 

Computing our limits of integration, we get

| **$x$** | $-1$ | $1/3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **$u$** | $0$ | $8$ |

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1/3}\frac{7}{4}x\sqrt[3]{6x+6}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{8}\frac{7}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{6}(u-6)\cdot {u}^{1/3}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{7}{144}{\int }_{0}^{8}({u}^{4/3}-6{u}^{1/3})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{7}{144}{(\frac{1}{(7/3)}{u}^{7/3}-6\cdot \frac{1}{(4/3)}{u}^{4/3})|}_{0}^{8} \\  & =\frac{7}{144}{(\frac{3}{7}{u}^{7/3}-\frac{9}{2}{u}^{4/3})|}_{0}^{8} \\  & =\frac{7}{144}[(\frac{3}{7}\cdot {8}^{7/3}-\frac{9}{2}\cdot {8}^{4/3})-(\frac{3}{7}\cdot {0}^{7/3}-\frac{9}{2}\cdot {0}^{4/3})] \\  & =\frac{7}{144}(\frac{384}{7}-72) \\  & =\frac{7}{144}\cdot (-\frac{120}{7}) \\  & =-\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
